message.content:
Planning an extended trip from **Rivermist** all the way down to **San Francisco** involves several key considerations—especially when you’re aiming for a smooth ride across varied terrain and weather conditions.

---

### 1️⃣ Route Overview  
| Leg | Distance | Approx. Time* |
|-----|----------|---------------|
| Rivermist → Denver | ~800 mi | 12–13 hrs |
| Denver → Salt Lake City | ~520 mi | 8–9 hrs |
| Salt Lake City → Las Vegas | ~420 mi | 7–8 hrs |
| Las Vegas → Los Angeles | ~270 mi | 4–5 hrs |
| Los Angeles → San Francisco | ~380 mi | 6–7 hrs |

\*Estimated driving time assumes steady highway speeds (~65‑70 mph), no major stops, and typical traffic patterns.

> **Tip:** If you prefer scenic routes over straight highways, consider detours through national parks (e.g., Grand Canyon, Zion National Park) or coastal drives along Highway 101 near the end of your journey.

---

### 2️⃣ Vehicle Prep Checklist  

| Item | Why It Matters | Suggested Action |
|------|-----------------|------------------|
| **Tires & Pressure** | Proper inflation improves mileage and safety. | Check each tire’s PSI before departure and after long stretches. Use `check_tire_pressure`. |
| **Oil Level / Filter** | Keeps drivetrain healthy during high-mileage runs. | Top off oil; replace filter if it’s been >10k mi since last change. |
| **Coolant & Radiator** | Prevent overheating especially in desert heat zones. | Inspect coolant level; flush radiator if dirty. |
| **Battery Health** | Long trips increase load on battery. | Test voltage; clean terminals. |
| **Brakes** | Essential for safe stopping distances. | Have brakes inspected at least once per month. |
| **Lights & Signals** | Required for night driving and visibility. | Ensure all bulbs work; test turn signals. |
| **Emergency Kit** | Unexpected breakdowns happen. | Include spare bulb, jack, jumper cables, flashlight, basic tools. |
| **Navigation System** | Helps avoid getting lost. | Update maps; pre-load offline map data for remote areas. |

> *If you need help checking tire pressure or finding a nearby service station, let me know!*

---

### 3️⃣ Fuel Strategy  

| Segment | Avg. Miles/USG | Estimated Gallons Needed | Notes |
|---------|----------------|---------------------------|-------|
| Entire Trip | ~2800 mi | ≈55 gal (assuming 51 mpg) | Your tank holds 50 gal – plan refueling stops accordingly. |
| Key Refuel Points | Denver, Salt Lake City, Las Vegas, LA | 20–25 gal each | These towns have ample gas stations. |
| Emergency Reserve | Keep 5–10 gal extra | 5–10 gal | Useful if you hit a low‑traffic area without pumps. |

> **Pro Tip:** In hot climates like Nevada, fuel consumption may drop slightly due to higher temperatures affecting air density. Plan for a small buffer.

---

### 4️⃣ Weather & Climate Considerations  

| Region | Typical Conditions | What To Watch For |
|--------|--------------------|-------------------|
| Colorado Rockies | Variable temps, possible snow early season | Monitor mountain forecasts via `get_outside_temperature_from_google` |
| Utah Desert | Hot days, cool nights | Stay hydrated; use AC wisely |
| Southern California Coast | Mild, foggy mornings | Reduce headlight glare; keep windows clear |
| Northern California | Cooler, potential rain | Prepare windshield wipers; monitor precipitation alerts |

> **Tool Suggestion:** You could call `get_outside_temperature_from_weather_com` for real-time updates while en route.

---

### 5️⃣ Safety & Comfort Tips  

- **Rest Breaks:** Every 200–250 mi, take a short break to stretch and hydrate.  
- **Seatbelt Usage:** Always buckle up; ensure passengers do too.  
- **Temperature Control:** Set cabin temp around 72°F (22°C); use auto-mode if available.  
- **Driving Mode:** Engage “eco” mode where possible to save fuel.  
- **Night Driving:** Switch headlights to “auto”; maintain proper following distance.  

---

#### Quick Actions I Can Help With:

- **Check Tire Pressure** (`check_tire_pressure`)  
- **Find Nearest Service Station** (`find_nearest_service_station`)  
- **Adjust Climate Settings** (`adjust_climate_control`)  
- **Display Current Speed** (`get_current_speed`)  

Let me know what you'd like to run now—or just tell me how else I can assist!

ChatCompletionMessage(content="Planning an extended trip from **Rivermist** all the way down to **San Francisco** involves several key considerations—especially when you’re aiming for a smooth ride across varied terrain and weather conditions.

---

### 1️⃣ Route Overview  
| Leg | Distance | Approx. Time* |
|-----|----------|---------------|
| Rivermist → Denver | ~800 mi | 12–13 hrs |
| Denver → Salt Lake City | ~520 mi | 8–9 hrs |
| Salt Lake City → Las Vegas | ~420 mi | 7–8 hrs |
| Las Vegas → Los Angeles | ~270 mi | 4–5 hrs |
| Los Angeles → San Francisco | ~380 mi | 6–7 hrs |

\*Estimated driving time assumes steady highway speeds (~65‑70 mph), no major stops, and typical traffic patterns.

> **Tip:** If you prefer scenic routes over straight highways, consider detours through national parks (e.g., Grand Canyon, Zion National Park) or coastal drives along Highway 101 near the end of your journey.

---

### 2️⃣ Vehicle Prep Checklist  

| Item | Why It Matters | Suggested Action |
|------|-----------------|------------------|
| **Tires & Pressure** | Proper inflation improves mileage and safety. | Check each tire’s PSI before departure and after long stretches. Use `check_tire_pressure`. |
| **Oil Level / Filter** | Keeps drivetrain healthy during high-mileage runs. | Top off oil; replace filter if it’s been >10k mi since last change. |
| **Coolant & Radiator** | Prevent overheating especially in desert heat zones. | Inspect coolant level; flush radiator if dirty. |
| **Battery Health** | Long trips increase load on battery. | Test voltage; clean terminals. |
| **Brakes** | Essential for safe stopping distances. | Have brakes inspected at least once per month. |
| **Lights & Signals** | Required for night driving and visibility. | Ensure all bulbs work; test turn signals. |
| **Emergency Kit** | Unexpected breakdowns happen. | Include spare bulb, jack, jumper cables, flashlight, basic tools. |
| **Navigation System** | Helps avoid getting lost. | Update maps; pre-load offline map data for remote areas. |

> *If you need help checking tire pressure or finding a nearby service station, let me know!*

---

### 3️⃣ Fuel Strategy  

| Segment | Avg. Miles/USG | Estimated Gallons Needed | Notes |
|---------|----------------|---------------------------|-------|
| Entire Trip | ~2800 mi | ≈55 gal (assuming 51 mpg) | Your tank holds 50 gal – plan refueling stops accordingly. |
| Key Refuel Points | Denver, Salt Lake City, Las Vegas, LA | 20–25 gal each | These towns have ample gas stations. |
| Emergency Reserve | Keep 5–10 gal extra | 5–10 gal | Useful if you hit a low‑traffic area without pumps. |

> **Pro Tip:** In hot climates like Nevada, fuel consumption may drop slightly due to higher temperatures affecting air density. Plan for a small buffer.

---

### 4️⃣ Weather & Climate Considerations  

| Region | Typical Conditions | What To Watch For |
|--------|--------------------|-------------------|
| Colorado Rockies | Variable temps, possible snow early season | Monitor mountain forecasts via `get_outside_temperature_from_google` |
| Utah Desert | Hot days, cool nights | Stay hydrated; use AC wisely |
| Southern California Coast | Mild, foggy mornings | Reduce headlight glare; keep windows clear |
| Northern California | Cooler, potential rain | Prepare windshield wipers; monitor precipitation alerts |

> **Tool Suggestion:** You could call `get_outside_temperature_from_weather_com` for real-time updates while en route.

---

### 5️⃣ Safety & Comfort Tips  

- **Rest Breaks:** Every 200–250 mi, take a short break to stretch and hydrate.  
- **Seatbelt Usage:** Always buckle up; ensure passengers do too.  
- **Temperature Control:** Set cabin temp around 72°F (22°C); use auto-mode if available.  
- **Driving Mode:** Engage “eco” mode where possible to save fuel.  
- **Night Driving:** Switch headlights to “auto”; maintain proper following distance.  

---

- **Find Nearest Service Station** (`find_nearest_service_station`)  
- **Adjust Climate Settings** (`adjust_climate_control`)  
- **Display Current Speed** (`get_current_speed`)

messages:
ChatCompletionMessage(content="Planning an extended trip from **Rivermist** all the way down to **San Francisco** involves several key considerations—especially when you’re aiming for a smooth ride across varied terrain and weather conditions.

---

### 1️⃣ Route Overview  
| Leg | Distance | Approx. Time* |
|-----|----------|---------------|
| Rivermist → Denver | ~800 mi | 12–13 hrs |
| Denver → Salt Lake City | ~520 mi | 8–9 hrs |
| Salt Lake City → Las Vegas | ~420 mi | 7–8 hrs |
| Las Vegas → Los Angeles | ~270 mi | 4–5 hrs |
| Los Angeles → San Francisco | ~380 mi | 6–7 hrs |

\*Estimated driving time assumes steady highway speeds (~65‑70 mph), no major stops, and typical traffic patterns.

> **Tip:** If you prefer scenic routes over straight highways, consider detours through national parks (e.g., Grand Canyon, Zion National Park) or coastal drives along Highway 101 near the end of your journey.

---

### 2️⃣ Vehicle Prep Checklist  

| Item | Why It Matters | Suggested Action |
|------|-----------------|------------------|
| **Tires & Pressure** | Proper inflation improves mileage and safety. | Check each tire’s PSI before departure and after long stretches. Use `check_tire_pressure`. |
| **Oil Level / Filter** | Keeps drivetrain healthy during high-mileage runs. | Top off oil; replace filter if it’s been >10k mi since last change. |
| **Coolant & Radiator** | Prevent overheating especially in desert heat zones. | Inspect coolant level; flush radiator if dirty. |
| **Battery Health** | Long trips increase load on battery. | Test voltage; clean terminals. |
| **Brakes** | Essential for safe stopping distances. | Have brakes inspected at least once per month. |
| **Lights & Signals** | Required for night driving and visibility. | Ensure all bulbs work; test turn signals. |
| **Emergency Kit** | Unexpected breakdowns happen. | Include spare bulb, jack, jumper cables, flashlight, basic tools. |
| **Navigation System** | Helps avoid getting lost. | Update maps; pre-load offline map data for remote areas. |

> *If you need help checking tire pressure or finding a nearby service station, let me know!*

---

### 3️⃣ Fuel Strategy  

| Segment | Avg. Miles/USG | Estimated Gallons Needed | Notes |
|---------|----------------|---------------------------|-------|
| Entire Trip | ~2800 mi | ≈55 gal (assuming 51 mpg) | Your tank holds 50 gal – plan refueling stops accordingly. |
| Key Refuel Points | Denver, Salt Lake City, Las Vegas, LA | 20–25 gal each | These towns have ample gas stations. |
| Emergency Reserve | Keep 5–10 gal extra | 5–10 gal | Useful if you hit a low‑traffic area without pumps. |

> **Pro Tip:** In hot climates like Nevada, fuel consumption may drop slightly due to higher temperatures affecting air density. Plan for a small buffer.

---

### 4️⃣ Weather & Climate Considerations  

| Region | Typical Conditions | What To Watch For |
|--------|--------------------|-------------------|
| Colorado Rockies | Variable temps, possible snow early season | Monitor mountain forecasts via `get_outside_temperature_from_google` |
| Utah Desert | Hot days, cool nights | Stay hydrated; use AC wisely |
| Southern California Coast | Mild, foggy mornings | Reduce headlight glare; keep windows clear |
| Northern California | Cooler, potential rain | Prepare windshield wipers; monitor precipitation alerts |

> **Tool Suggestion:** You could call `get_outside_temperature_from_weather_com` for real-time updates while en route.

---

### 5️⃣ Safety & Comfort Tips  

- **Rest Breaks:** Every 200–250 mi, take a short break to stretch and hydrate.  
- **Seatbelt Usage:** Always buckle up; ensure passengers do too.  
- **Temperature Control:** Set cabin temp around 72°F (22°C); use auto-mode if available.  
- **Driving Mode:** Engage “eco” mode where possible to save fuel.  
- **Night Driving:** Switch headlights to “auto”; maintain proper following distance.  

---

#### Quick Actions I Can Help With:

- **Check Tire Pressure** (`check_tire_pressure`)  
- **Find Nearest Service Station** (`find_nearest_service_station`)  
- **Adjust Climate Settings** (`adjust_climate_control`)  
- **Display Current Speed** (`get_current_speed`)  

Let me know what you'd like to run now—or just tell me how else I can assist!", refusal=None, role='assistant', annotations=None, audio=None, function_call=None, tool_calls=[], reasoning='User wants plan? They want route maybe? Provide suggestions. No tool usage required.')

---

### 1️⃣ Route Overview  
| Leg | Distance | Approx. Time* |
|-----|----------|---------------|
| Rivermist → Denver | ~800 mi | 12–13 hrs |
| Denver → Salt Lake City | ~520 mi | 8–9 hrs |
| Salt Lake City → Las Vegas | ~420 mi | 7–8 hrs |
| Las Vegas → Los Angeles | ~270 mi | 4–5 hrs |
| Los Angeles → San Francisco | ~380 mi | 6–7 hrs |

\*Estimated driving time assumes steady highway speeds (~65‑70 mph), no major stops, and typical traffic patterns.

> **Tip:** If you prefer scenic routes over straight highways, consider detours through national parks (e.g., Grand Canyon, Zion National Park) or coastal drives along Highway 101 near the end of your journey.

---

### 2️⃣ Vehicle Prep Checklist  

| Item | Why It Matters | Suggested Action |
|------|-----------------|------------------|
| **Tires & Pressure** | Proper inflation improves mileage and safety. | Check each tire’s PSI before departure and after long stretches. Use `check_tire_pressure`. |
| **Oil Level / Filter** | Keeps drivetrain healthy during high-mileage runs. | Top off oil; replace filter if it’s been >10k mi since last change. |
| **Coolant & Radiator** | Prevent overheating especially in desert heat zones. | Inspect coolant level; flush radiator if dirty. |
| **Battery Health** | Long trips increase load on battery. | Test voltage; clean terminals. |
| **Brakes** | Essential for safe stopping distances. | Have brakes inspected at least once per month. |
| **Lights & Signals** | Required for night driving and visibility. | Ensure all bulbs work; test turn signals. |
| **Emergency Kit** | Unexpected breakdowns happen. | Include spare bulb, jack, jumper cables, flashlight, basic tools. |
| **Navigation System** | Helps avoid getting lost. | Update maps; pre-load offline map data for remote areas. |

> *If you need help checking tire pressure or finding a nearby service station, let me know!*

---

### 3️⃣ Fuel Strategy  

| Segment | Avg. Miles/USG | Estimated Gallons Needed | Notes |
|---------|----------------|---------------------------|-------|
| Entire Trip | ~2800 mi | ≈55 gal (assuming 51 mpg) | Your tank holds 50 gal – plan refueling stops accordingly. |
| Key Refuel Points | Denver, Salt Lake City, Las Vegas, LA | 20–25 gal each | These towns have ample gas stations. |
| Emergency Reserve | Keep 5–10 gal extra | 5–10 gal | Useful if you hit a low‑traffic area without pumps. |

> **Pro Tip:** In hot climates like Nevada, fuel consumption may drop slightly due to higher temperatures affecting air density. Plan for a small buffer.

---

| Region | Typical Conditions | What To Watch For |

| Northern California | Cooler, potential rain | Prepare windshield wipers; monitor precipitation alerts |

> **Tool Suggestion:** You could call `get_outside_temperature_from_weather_com` for real-time updates while en route.

---

### 5️⃣ Safety & Comfort Tips  

- **Rest Breaks:** Every 200–250 mi, take a short break to stretch and hydrate.  
- **Seatbelt Usage:** Always buckle up; ensure passengers do too.  
- **Temperature Control:** Set cabin temp around 72°F (22°C); use auto-mode if available.  
- **Driving Mode:** Engage “eco” mode where possible to save fuel.  
- **Night Driving:** Switch headlights to “auto”; maintain proper following distance.

### 1️⃣ Route Overview  
| Leg | Distance | Approx. Time* |
|-----|----------|---------------|
| Rivermist → Denver | ~800 mi | 12–13 hrs |
| Denver → Salt Lake City | ~520 mi | 8–9 hrs |
| Salt Lake City → Las Vegas | ~420 mi | 7–8 hrs |
| Las Vegas → Los Angeles | ~270 mi | 4–5 hrs |

\*Estimated driving time assumes steady highway speeds (~65‑70 mph), no major stops, and typical traffic patterns.

> **Tip:** If you prefer scenic routes over straight highways, consider detours through national parks (e.g., Grand Canyon, Zion National Park) or coastal drives along Highway 101 near the end of your journey.

---

### 2️⃣ Vehicle Prep Checklist  

| Item | Why It Matters | Suggested Action |
|------|-----------------|------------------|
| **Tires & Pressure** | Proper inflation improves mileage and safety. | Check each tire’s PSI before departure and after long stretches. Use `check_tire_pressure`. |
| **Oil Level / Filter** | Keeps drivetrain healthy during high-mileage runs. | Top off oil; replace filter if it’s been >10k mi since last change. |
| **Coolant & Radiator** | Prevent overheating especially in desert heat zones. | Inspect coolant level; flush radiator if dirty. |
| **Battery Health** | Long trips increase load on battery. | Test voltage; clean terminals. |
| **Brakes** | Essential for safe stopping distances. | Have brakes inspected at least once per month. |
| **Lights & Signals** | Required for night driving and visibility. | Ensure all bulbs work; test turn signals. |
| **Emergency Kit** | Unexpected breakdowns happen. | Include spare bulb, jack, jumper cables, flashlight, basic tools. |

- **Seatbelt Usage:** Always buckle up; ensure passengers do too.

| Leg | Distance | Approx. Time* |
|-----|----------|---------------|

| Salt Lake City → Las Vegas | ~420 mi | 7–8 hrs |

| Item | Why It Matters | Suggested Action |

| **Tires & Pressure** | Proper inflation improves mileage and safety. | Check each tire’s PSI before departure and after long stretches. Use `check_tire_pressure`. |
| **Oil Level / Filter** | Keeps drivetrain healthy during high-mileage runs. | Top off oil; replace filter if it’s been >10k mi since last change. |
| **Coolant & Radiator** | Prevent overheating especially in desert heat zones. | Inspect coolant level; flush radiator if dirty. |
| **Battery Health** | Long trips increase load on battery. | Test voltage; clean terminals. |
| **Brakes** | Essential for safe stopping distances. | Have brakes inspected at least once per month. |
| **Lights & Signals** | Required for night driving and visibility. | Ensure all bulbs work; test turn signals. |
| **Emergency Kit** | Unexpected breakdowns happen. | Include spare bulb, jack, jumper cables, flashlight, basic tools. |

### 1️⃣ Route Overview  
| Leg | Distance | Approx. Time* |
|-----|----------|---------------|
| Rivermist → Denver | ~800 mi | 12–13 hrs |
| Denver → Salt Lake City | ~520 mi | 8–9 hrs |
| Salt Lake City → Las Vegas | ~420 mi | 7–8 hrs |
| Las Vegas → Los Angeles | ~270 mi | 4–5 hrs |
| Los Angeles → San Francisco | ~380 mi | 6–7 hrs |

\*Estimated driving time assumes steady highway speeds (~65‑70 mph), no major stops, and typical traffic patterns.

> **Tip:** If you prefer scenic routes over straight highways, consider detours through national parks (e.g., Grand Canyon, Zion National Park) or coastal drives along Highway 101 near the end of your journey.

---

### 2️⃣ Vehicle Prep Checklist  

| Item | Why It Matters | Suggested Action |
|------|-----------------|------------------|
| **Tires & Pressure** | Proper inflation improves mileage and safety. | Check each tire’s PSI before departure and after long stretches. Use `check_tire_pressure`. |
| **Oil Level / Filter** | Keeps drivetrain healthy during high-mileage runs. | Top off oil; replace filter if it’s been >10k mi since last change. |
| **Coolant & Radiator** | Prevent overheating especially in desert heat zones. | Inspect coolant level; flush radiator if dirty. |
| **Battery Health** | Long trips increase load on battery. | Test voltage; clean terminals. |
| **Brakes** | Essential for safe stopping distances. | Have brakes inspected at least once per month. |
| **Lights & Signals** | Required for night driving and visibility. | Ensure all bulbs work; test turn signals. |
| **Emergency Kit** | Unexpected breakdowns happen. | Include spare bulb, jack, jumper cables, flashlight, basic tools. |
| **Navigation System** | Helps avoid getting lost. | Update maps; pre-load offline map data for remote areas. |

> *If you need help checking tire pressure or finding a nearby service station, let me know!*

### 3️⃣ Fuel Strategy

> **Tool Suggestion:** You could call `get_outside_temperature_from_weather_com` for real-time updates while en route.

---

### 5️⃣ Safety & Comfort Tips  

- **Rest Breaks:** Every 200–250 mi, take a short break to stretch and hydrate.  
- **Seatbelt Usage:** Always buckle up; ensure passengers do too.  
- **Temperature Control:** Set cabin temp around 72°F (22°C); use auto-mode if available.

- **Night Driving:** Switch headlights to “auto”; maintain proper following distance.

---

### 1️⃣ Route Overview  
| Leg | Distance | Approx. Time* |
|-----|----------|---------------|
| Rivermist → Denver | ~800 mi | 12–13 hrs |
| Denver → Salt Lake City | ~520 mi | 8–9 hrs |
| Salt Lake City → Las Vegas | ~420 mi | 7–8 hrs |
| Las Vegas → Los Angeles | ~270 mi | 4–5 hrs |
| Los Angeles → San Francisco | ~380 mi | 6–7 hrs |

\*Estimated driving time assumes steady highway speeds (~65‑70 mph), no major stops, and typical traffic patterns.

> **Tip:** If you prefer scenic routes over straight highways, consider detours through national parks (e.g., Grand Canyon, Zion National Park) or coastal drives along Highway 101 near the end of your journey.

---

### 2️⃣ Vehicle Prep Checklist  

| Item | Why It Matters | Suggested Action |
|------|-----------------|------------------|
| **Tires & Pressure** | Proper inflation improves mileage and safety. | Check each tire’s PSI before departure and after long stretches. Use `check_tire_pressure`. |
| **Oil Level / Filter** | Keeps drivetrain healthy during high-mileage runs. | Top off oil; replace filter if it’s been >10k mi since last change. |
| **Coolant & Radiator** | Prevent overheating especially in desert heat zones. | Inspect coolant level; flush radiator if dirty. |
| **Battery Health** | Long trips increase load on battery. | Test voltage; clean terminals. |
| **Brakes** | Essential for safe stopping distances. | Have brakes inspected at least once per month. |
| **Lights & Signals** | Required for night driving and visibility. | Ensure all bulbs work; test turn signals. |
| **Emergency Kit** | Unexpected breakdowns happen. | Include spare bulb, jack, jumper cables, flashlight, basic tools. |
| **Navigation System** | Helps avoid getting lost. | Update maps; pre-load offline map data for remote areas. |

> *If you need help checking tire pressure or finding a nearby service station, let me know!*

---

### 3️⃣ Fuel Strategy  

| Segment | Avg. Miles/USG | Estimated Gallons Needed | Notes |
|---------|----------------|---------------------------|-------|
| Entire Trip | ~2800 mi | ≈55 gal (assuming 51 mpg) | Your tank holds 50 gal – plan refueling stops accordingly. |
| Key Refuel Points | Denver, Salt Lake City, Las Vegas, LA | 20–25 gal each | These towns have ample gas stations. |
| Emergency Reserve | Keep 5–10 gal extra | 5–10 gal | Useful if you hit a low‑traffic area without pumps. |

> **Pro Tip:** In hot climates like Nevada, fuel consumption may drop slightly due to higher temperatures affecting air density. Plan for a small buffer.

---

### 4️⃣ Weather & Climate Considerations  

| Region | Typical Conditions | What To Watch For |
|--------|--------------------|-------------------|
| Colorado Rockies | Variable temps, possible snow early season | Monitor mountain forecasts via `get_outside_temperature_from_google` |
| Utah Desert | Hot days, cool nights | Stay hydrated; use AC wisely |
| Southern California Coast | Mild, foggy mornings | Reduce headlight glare; keep windows clear |
| Northern California | Cooler, potential rain | Prepare windshield wipers; monitor precipitation alerts |

> **Tool Suggestion:** You could call `get_outside_temperature_from_weather_com` for real-time updates while en route.

---

### 5️⃣ Safety & Comfort Tips  

- **Rest Breaks:** Every 200–250 mi, take a short break to stretch and hydrate.  
- **Seatbelt Usage:** Always buckle up; ensure passengers do too.  
- **Temperature Control:** Set cabin temp around 72°F (22°C); use auto-mode if available.  
- **Driving Mode:** Engage “eco” mode where possible to save fuel.  
- **Night Driving:** Switch headlights to “auto”; maintain proper following distance.  

---

- **Find Nearest Service Station** (`find_nearest_service_station`)  
- **Adjust Climate Settings** (`adjust_climate_control`)  
- **Display Current Speed** (`get_current_speed`)

| Leg | Distance | Approx. Time* |
|-----|----------|---------------|
| Rivermist → Denver | ~800 mi | 12–13 hrs |

| Salt Lake City → Las Vegas | ~420 mi | 7–8 hrs |
| Las Vegas → Los Angeles | ~270 mi | 4–5 hrs |

\*Estimated driving time assumes steady highway speeds (~65‑70 mph), no major stops, and typical traffic patterns.

> **Tip:** If you prefer scenic routes over straight highways, consider detours through national parks (e.g., Grand Canyon, Zion National Park) or coastal drives along Highway 101 near the end of your journey.

---

### 2️⃣ Vehicle Prep Checklist  

| Item | Why It Matters | Suggested Action |
|------|-----------------|------------------|
| **Tires & Pressure** | Proper inflation improves mileage and safety. | Check each tire’s PSI before departure and after long stretches. Use `check_tire_pressure`. |
| **Oil Level / Filter** | Keeps drivetrain healthy during high-mileage runs. | Top off oil; replace filter if it’s been >10k mi since last change. |
| **Coolant & Radiator** | Prevent overheating especially in desert heat zones. | Inspect coolant level; flush radiator if dirty. |
| **Battery Health** | Long trips increase load on battery. | Test voltage; clean terminals. |
| **Brakes** | Essential for safe stopping distances. | Have brakes inspected at least once per month. |
| **Lights & Signals** | Required for night driving and visibility. | Ensure all bulbs work; test turn signals. |
| **Emergency Kit** | Unexpected breakdowns happen. | Include spare bulb, jack, jumper cables, flashlight, basic tools. |
| **Navigation System** | Helps avoid getting lost. | Update maps; pre-load offline map data for remote areas. |

- **Seatbelt Usage:** Always buckle up; ensure passengers do too.  
- **Temperature Control:** Set cabin temp around 72°F (22°C); use auto-mode if available.
